appraisal_events.evidence: « c'était l'idée qu'elle était coupable » se substitue peu à peu « à l'idée qu'Albertine était innocente » ; « je passerais assez rapidement de la certitude de l'innocence d'Albertine à la certitude de sa culpabilité » ; son nom rejoint ceux de Guermantes, de Swann, du lift, vidés de leur charme ; « la puissance douloureuse de la culpabilité d'Albertine serait renvoyée hors de moi par l'habitude » ; « pour que je pusse oublier ces idées et enfin oublier Albertine elle-même ».
appraisal_events.explanation: The retrospective narrator stages Albertine's demotion twice over: guilt replaces innocence as the settled ground of his consciousness, and her name is enrolled among the words habit has emptied, so that she is already headed toward the indifferent memory the passage names as its goal. The diminishment is presented as accomplished fact, not as one option among several.

appraisal_events.evidence: « un médecin de l'âme qui m'eût visité eût trouvé que, pour le reste, mon chagrin lui-même allait mieux » ; le tunnel noir « s'interrompait brusquement d'un intervalle de soleil » sur « un univers souriant et bleu » et « comme une fleur qui s'entr'ouvre j'éprouvais la fraîcheur rajeunissante d'une exfoliation » ; « Je dus souffrir beaucoup pendant cette période-là, mais je me rends compte qu'il fallait que ce fût ainsi. On ne guérit d'une souffrance qu'à condition de l'éprouver pleinement. »
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrating self diagnoses the suffering self as convalescent and explicitly ratifies the martyrdom as the necessary road to cure, which locally raises him from victim to physician of his own case. The gain is real but qualified: the passage keeps him inside jealousy, suspicion, and a fear that his pain is now cardiac, so the elevation is prospective rather than attained.

status_effects.explanation: She passes definitively from presumed innocent to presumed guilty in the narrator's settled conviction, and cannot answer; even the tenderness that returns folds her vice into itself as « une cause d'amour ».
Still alive in him at the start, she is by the end slated for expulsion: habit will carry her guilt « hors de moi », and the closing clause makes forgetting her the aim of the whole process.

He gains ground on his grief: the idea of her death has conquered the place held by the idea of her life, the sunlit interval brings a rejuvenating exfoliation, and he can now describe his own suffering as a treatable and necessary phase.

ambiguities: The passage diminishes Albertine while openly discrediting the verdict it reaches: the certainty of her guilt is said to grow because it becomes habitual and therefore less painful, and the objections to it are said to have been raised only by the wish not to suffer. The diminishment is real as a narrated process, but the narrator withholds endorsement of guilt as fact.

The narrator's improvement is offered and undercut in the same movement: the luminous interval « ne me faisai[t] peut-être que mieux prendre conscience de mon amour », the period is called « le martyre », and jealousy still resurges through Andrée as a mere prête-nom, so the elevation must be read as mixed rather than as achieved renewal.
